_readme: Machine-refreshable metric store (wave 13). Keys are provenance IDs (content/provenance.md). Values are refreshed weekly by .github/workflows/metrics-refresh.yml from each source repo's .portfolio/metrics.json — via a reviewed PR, never a direct commit. Hand-edit only to correct an error; the narrative provenance record stays in content/provenance.md.

style-maitri:intent-accuracy.note: Corrected 2026-08-06: the prior 94.4%/n=378 value traced to reports/model_eval_20260731T060759Z.md, which is gitignored and was never committed (confirmed via git ls-files — no such file exists in any commit). This entry, the products.ts card, and the case-study body had all diverged from the already-reverted, git-committed figure; only the case-study body had actually been fixed (see provenance.md's Wave 19 section) — this manifest entry and the homepage card were simply never updated at the same time. reports/final_scorecard_2026-07-12.txt:109 reads: 'intent all-exact    93.8%  (min 88.0%, n=211) PASS'.

gold-rate-tracker:headline.label: Naive baseline vs. ML model (199-fold backtest)
gold-rate-tracker:headline.value: Naive wins — ships the honest baseline, not the model
gold-rate-tracker:headline.note: data/backtest.json is bot-refreshed continuously and has moved on since this pin (now 204 folds as of 2026-07-26). The qualitative 'naive wins' claim holds at every snapshot checked. Wave-18 reconciliation fixed an internal-consistency bug in the case study: the Wilcoxon p and direction-accuracy figures shown alongside this pinned commit's MAE numbers had drifted in from a different (194-fold) snapshot — both are now pinned to this same commit_sha (0.0 as stored, rendered as 'p < 0.001' per GG's never-render-p-approx-0 instruction; direction accuracy 50.75%). Commit a4d892c itself is real and tracked (chore: update backtest results [skip ci] (#247), committed 2026-07-19T10:46:27+05:30; backtest_run_at 2026-07-19T05:12:36 UTC).
